title: Sweep applies the corrected ?? snapshot rule to the name only — the fresh invite still goes to the stale contact_email/phone
evidence:
-       rc.contact_name,
+       -- RC4.3: the EFFECTIVE referee name (corrected ?? snapshot) — the
+       -- invite/reminder copy addresses the referee by name, and a
+       -- landlord-corrected name must flow into the fresh invite (§8.3).
+       COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_name, ''), rc.contact_name) AS contact_name,
        rc.contact_email,
        rc.contact_phone,
detail: correct_reference_call writes the new address into corrected_email/corrected_phone and re-queues, but this SELECT (the sweep that owns the fresh invite) still reads raw contact_email/contact_phone. After a correction the invite is delivered to the old, already-failing address while greeting the corrected name — the correction's core purpose is defeated.
recommended_fix: Apply the same COALESCE(NULLIF(corrected_x, ''), contact_x) to contact_email and contact_phone in sweep_due_reference_calls.sql, or coalesce downstream at the send site.

title: verify_vacancy_active precheck fails open: 0 rows, not-owned, and DB errors all fall through to action()
detail: The ownership check above 404s on every non-single-row outcome, but the vacancy check's `_` arm treats "vacancy absent / not owned by this landlord / query error" as "vacancy active" and runs the mutation. A mismatched vacancy_id in the URL sails through the prechecks.
recommended_fix: Mirror the ownership-check shape: only `Ok(Returned(_, [r])) if not r.is_archived` should reach action(); 0 rows and Error must return 404/500 before mutating.

title: do_correct treats a 0-row application-trio UPDATE as success — row corrected, trio silently unchanged, audit still written
evidence:
case
                  update_trio(tx, app_uuid, vacancy_uuid, row.ref_slot, trio)
                {
                  Error(err) -> Error(DbFailure(err))
                  Ok(_) ->
                    case
                      audit_log.create(
...
fn row_count(returned: pog.Returned(a)) -> Int {
  list.length(returned.rows)
}
detail: update_trio maps to the affected-row count; Ok(0) falls through to the audit and a 200 "corrected": true. With the fail-open vacancy precheck (mismatched vacancy_id) the reference_call row is corrected while the application's trio is not — 200 success, silent divergence, wrong audit From/To.
recommended_fix: Treat a 0-row trio update as a transaction-aborting error (e.g. extend ActionError) so the correction cannot commit without updating the application trio.

title: Exhaustion notification still uses the raw contact_name — after a correction it announces "Couldn't reach <stale name>"
detail: find_reference_call_by_send_ref and get_form_context_by_form_token still select raw rc.contact_name while sweep_due_reference_calls was switched to corrected ?? snapshot. The exhaustion path (which fires only after a correction ran) greets the landlord with the name they just corrected.
recommended_fix: Apply the corrected ?? snapshot coalesce to contact_name in find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql and get_form_context_by_form_token.sql, or coalesce at the notification call sites.

title: Fraud-signal stamp failure is log-only in the form exhaustion path but Sentry-captured in the webhook path
evidence:
case sql.stamp_referee_contact_invalid(config.db, id_uuid) {
        Ok(_) -> Nil
        Error(err) ->
          wisp.log_error(
            "reference wrong-person: fraud-signal stamp failed: "
            <> string.inspect(err),
          )
detail: The webhook exhaustion captures ReferenceWebhookStampFailed via Sentry; exhaust_wrong_person only logs. The referee_contact_invalid signal is a compliance-relevant write — a silent failure is invisible outside raw logs and never retried.
recommended_fix: Mirror the webhook path in exhaust_wrong_person: capture a Sentry background event on stamp failure so the lost signal is visible.

title: substitute_reference_call INSERT never sets status — the "created queued" claim rests on an unseen schema default
evidence:
+  INSERT INTO reference_call (
+    application_id, ref_slot, owner_label,
+    contact_name, contact_email, contact_phone,
+    next_attempt_at
+  )
+  SELECT application_id, ref_slot, owner_label,
+         $3, NULLIF($4, ''), NULLIF($5, ''),
+         now()
+  FROM guard
detail: Comments and the audit claim the successor is born 'queued' (To: "queued"), and idempotency depends on the successor being a live state in the partial unique index, but the INSERT omits status/outcome/correction_cycles entirely. If the column default is not 'queued' the row is invisible to the sweep and the audit lies.
recommended_fix: Set status = 'queued'::reference_call_status explicitly in the INSERT (and any other columns the design assumes a default for).

title: substitute's ON CONFLICT predicate must textually match the live-slot partial unique index, which is not in this diff
evidence:
+  ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (
+    'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected',
+    'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial'
+  )
+  DO NOTHING
detail: PostgreSQL matches a partial unique index only when the ON CONFLICT WHERE predicate is identical to the index predicate. The migration defining this index is absent from the chunk; any drift in the terminal-status list (e.g. a missing 'skipped') makes every substitution statement error at runtime.
recommended_fix: Verify the migration's partial unique index predicate matches this list character-for-character (including all terminal statuses) before merging.
